sulfuricresonance.ponder.combustion_belt: Heating Items on a Combustion Belt
Create a Combustion Belt between aligned Thermochemical Shafts using the Combustion Belt Connector
Marked Combustion Belts transport items continuously like ordinary Create belts
Heat must enter through a genuine physical connection to one of the Belt's pulley shafts
This heated Molten Rotor and Conduit supply Superheated heat directly into the starting pulley
The selected live heat tier is shared across every marked segment in this Belt chain
A recipe advances only while its item is moving, sufficient heat is present, and new qualifying segments are crossed
This five-segment scene is condensed; real recipes still require their configured distance and processing time
Losing the heat source does not stop transport, but processing immediately stops advancing
Restore sufficient heat before retained progress decays to continue the same process
When both distance and time requirements are met, the moving input converts into the recipe output
Heat below a recipe's minimum tier carries the input through unchanged
A directly adjacent heated Combustion Belt pulley can relay heat into another marked pulley, but heat never crosses a Belt body from one end to the other

A Rotation Speed Controller is the best way to tune processing: slower Belts give items more heated time, while faster Belts increase throughput only when the recipe still meets both its distance and time requirements
Reactive Heat follows one physical chain: generate, transmit, renew, route, then process
sulfuricresonance.ponder.living_ember_la: Linking and Reading the Living Ember Lamp
The Living Ember Lamp remotely displays the heat and fuel condition of one Molten Rotor Furnace
Before placing it, right-click the furnace while holding the Lamp
A pulsing blue outline marks the selected furnace while the linked Lamp is held
After placement, holding a Lamp from the same network outlines both the furnace and every connected Lamp
A cold or inactive furnace leaves the Lamp dark at level 0
Fading or Smouldering heat raises it smoothly to level 7
Kindled or Seething heat raises it smoothly to level 11
At Radiant heat, the Lamp reaches its steady level 13 glow
With 200 fuel ticks or less and no fuel queued, or during the final 200 ticks of heated cooldown after fuel reaches zero, the Lamp pulses between levels 9 and 15
Cross-dimensional links can resolve normally. If a valid linked furnace is temporarily unavailable or unloaded, the Lamp keeps its saved connection and last target instead of force-loading it
Destroying the original furnace invalidates its stored identity, so the Lamp fades safely back to darkness
Breaking and replacing the furnace does not restore the link, even at the same position
sulfuricresonance.ponder.molten_rotor.op: The Molten Rotor Furnace converts stored heat into rotational force
Shafts can connect to either side of the furnace
At ambient temperature, the furnace remains idle until it reaches 300°C
Smouldering begins at 300°C and produces 32 RPM
Kindled begins at 500°C, raising output to 64 RPM
Seething begins at 800°C, producing 128 RPM and meeting the Superheated requirement
Radiant begins at 1300°C, producing 256 RPM and enabling Combustion recipes
The front gauge tracks chamber temperature as the furnace crosses each heat tier
Engineer's Goggles show temperature, heat state, stress capacity, generated speed, fuel and cooldown time
When fuel runs out, stored heat drains away and output slows through lower tiers before stopping
The Molten Rotor is the source; Thermochemical Shafts carry its rotation and heat into the network
sulfuricresonance.ponder.perforated_spri: Perforated Spritzer
Using the Perforated Spritzer
The Perforated Spritzer can store and disperse fluids in a downward fashion
It will hold up to 3500mB of any fluid
Once it reaches 3500mB, the Spritzer can begin spraying supported fluid on its own
Pipes and pumps are useful for keeping the internal tank supplied while it sprays
Filling the Spritzer to 3500mB arms its automatic spray cycle
...then it begins spraying the fluid downward automatically!
The Spritzer can hydrate farmland
...it can also water crops!
Crop growth can be nudged once the farmland below reaches moisture level 4; full hydration is not required
Mob Automation with the Perforated Spritzer
This setup uses a Perforated Spritzer to damage mobs and collect their drops
Sulfuric Acid applies Acid Burn and repeatedly damages living entities beneath the Spritzer
When the mob is defeated, its drops remain beneath the Spritzer
An Encased Fan pushes those dropped items toward the Funnel
The Funnel inserts the loot into the attached Chest automatically
Supplying Lava instead ignites entities caught beneath the Spritzer
Water has the opposite use, extinguishing burning entities below
Choose the supplied fluid to damage mobs, ignite them, or extinguish fire

sulfuricresonance.ponder.thermal_relay_s: Monitoring Heat with the Thermal Relay Switch
The Thermal Relay Switch turns Molten Rotor heat and fuel status into configurable redstone output.
Right-click a Molten Rotor Furnace with the relay item to add it to the selected network.
More furnaces can be selected before the relay is placed.
Placing the item completes the connection and stores the entire selected network.
Holding another connected relay item reveals the linked furnaces and matching placed relays.
Empty-hand right-click opens the control panel.
Custom Heat Output assigns independent redstone and glow values to Heated, Superheated, and Combustion states.
The relay supplies its configured analog signal on every side.
Heated: default signal 5, glow 1.
Superheated: default signal 10, glow 2.
Combustion: default signal 15, glow 3.
Players may choose any values within the limits: Heated 0–7, Superheated 0–12, Combustion 0–15, and glow 0–5.
This allows exact automation, including outputs that activate at only one heat tier.
The signal can control a Clutch, Redstone Link, warning system, or automated fuel supply.
Low Fuel Warning mode monitors every valid linked furnace and pulses when a qualifying furnace has ten seconds of fuel or less.
The heat scope can target Heated furnaces, Superheated and Combustion furnaces, or both ranges.
The configured redstone and glow warning pulse together: 10 ticks on, 10 ticks off.
In Custom Heat mode, the hottest valid furnace selects the output profile.
In Low Fuel mode, every furnace inside the selected heat scope is checked; one warning is enough to pulse the relay.
Breaking a linked furnace invalidates its stored identity. A replacement at the same coordinates does not inherit the link.
Unloaded furnace chunks are ignored without being force-loaded, while the saved connection remains available.
Sneak-right-click the placed relay to clear its network and immediately reset redstone and glow to zero.
One furnace network can support several relays, each with its own saved control profile.
sulfuricresonance.ponder.thermochemical_: Renewing a Thermochemical Route
Thermochemical Conduits transmit ordinary kinetic rotation through their internal shaft
They also renew the distance available to a physically connected thermochemical heat route
A Conduit does not generate heat and cannot collect it wirelessly from nearby machinery
Here, a heated Molten Rotor reaches the Conduit through a real Thermochemical Shaft connection
Once the Conduit is reached, it starts a fresh downstream allowance of ten transmission segments
More Thermochemical Shafts can now continue carrying both rotation and heat beyond it
A Wrench can rotate the Conduit between the X, Y, and Z axes even while it is connected
Rotating it away from the line breaks that physical route, so the downstream Shafts stop receiving rotation and heat
Rotate it back into alignment to restore the complete network immediately
Breaking any required Shaft also interrupts everything beyond the gap
Replace the missing Thermochemical Shaft to reconnect the downstream route
Use Conduits as renewal points, but keep every Shaft aligned and physically connected
After renewing the span, use a Thermochemical Gearbox when the route must turn, climb, or branch
Turning and Branching Thermochemical Routes
Thermochemical Gearboxes expose real rotational and thermochemical connections on all six faces
A heated Molten Rotor can enter one face through a physically aligned Thermochemical Shaft
The opposite face provides a straight-through output without requiring another block orientation
This route reaches its first Conduit through one Shaft, the Gearbox, and one more Shaft: exactly three cost-one nodes
The Conduit then renews the downstream allowance to ten transmission segments
With the west face used as input, all five remaining faces can operate as simultaneous output branches
The same block can route straight ahead, turn ninety degrees, and send the network vertically
Every branch receives the same heat tier and inherits the allowance remaining when the Gearbox was reached
These farther Shafts still carry ordinary rotation, but they are beyond the source-side heat allowance until a Conduit is reached
Breaking the source-side connection stops the Gearbox and every branch beyond it
Replace the missing Shaft and all physically connected branches resume immediately
Breaking one output branch interrupts only that branch while the other connected faces continue operating
A Gearbox costs one segment and routes heat without generating, multiplying, storing, or renewing it; only a Conduit renews allowance
Route a valid branch into a Combustion Belt pulley to turn the heat network into item processing
Routing Rotation and Thermochemical Heat
Thermochemical Shafts transmit ordinary kinetic rotation just like Create Shafts
They also carry thermochemical heat through a real, physically connected network
Ordinary Shafts cannot replace them inside a thermochemical route
Use a Wrench to rotate the Shaft between the X, Y, and Z axes, even while it is connected
Extend the line with more Thermochemical Shafts to carry rotation and heat together
From a Molten Rotor, the first Conduit must be reached within three Thermochemical Shafts
A Thermochemical Conduit renews the downstream shaft allowance
After a Conduit, up to ten transmission segments may continue before another renewal is needed
A Thermochemical Gearbox can turn or branch the route, but it does not renew the allowance
Breaking any required physical connection immediately interrupts thermochemical transmission
Reach a Thermochemical Conduit before the source-side transmission allowance is exhausted

sulfuricresonance.ponder.thermochemical_: Routing Heat Through Chain Drives
Thermochemical Link Drives carry rotation and thermochemical heat through the same physical chain segment
Neighbouring Link Drives connect sideways while their shaft axes stay available for machine and network connections
Feed one end through a Thermochemical Shaft and the chain carries the kinetic network across every linked drive
Thermochemical heat follows that same connected route instead of jumping wirelessly between Link Drives
Ordinary Create chain drives do not join this thermochemical chain; use Thermochemical Link Drives for the heat route
Link Drives relay supplied heat but do not generate it or renew route allowance; a Conduit still performs renewal
Every Link Drive keeps two axial shaft ports available, so one linked segment can accept or hand off rotation and thermochemical heat at several points
Goggles report how many of those shaft-side connections are occupied across the entire Link Drive segment
Treat the segment as one continuous physical route: any missing or misaligned Link Drive cuts off every downstream connection

Recipes always use a substrate and may additionally require a catalyst and auxiliary reagent
Item automation is intentionally limited to the top and back interfaces; the front, shaft side, acid side, and bottom are not item ports
The Chamber becomes READY only when its Sulfuric Acid amount, minimum heat tier, minimum RPM, ingredients, and output space are all satisfied
The GUI has Automatic and Manual operating modes: Automatic starts a READY recipe immediately, while Manual waits for the player to press Start
While processing, the input batch is locked against new insertion, but manually removing an input safely aborts and resets the reaction
sulfuricresonance.ponder.thermochemical_: Thermochemical Cogwheels

They can mesh mechanically with ordinary Create cogwheels, so the kinetic network can continue normally
Thermochemical heat does not cross into an ordinary Create cogwheel; use Thermochemical Cogwheels anywhere the heat route must continue
Cogwheels relay supplied heat but do not generate heat or renew thermochemical route allowance
sulfuricresonance.ponder.large_thermoche: Large Thermochemical Cogwheels provide the large-cog form of the same combined kinetic and thermochemical connection

sulfuricresonance.ponder.parallel_thermo: The Parallel Thermochemical Gearbox routes rotation and thermochemical heat through all six faces like the normal Thermochemical Gearbox

Use the Parallel variant when a compact branch needs that alternate output phase instead of treating it as a cosmetic gearbox
Thermochemical heat still follows the same physical connections and is unaffected by the rotational phase choice
Like the normal gearbox, it relays supplied heat but does not create heat or renew route allowance

Use the Crucible when a recipe specifically calls for CSR's heat-resistant basin processing path

sulfuricresonance.ponder.thermochemical_: Interrupting Heat and Rotation
The Thermochemical Clutch is an inline control point for both kinetic rotation and thermochemical heat
Without a redstone signal, both systems pass straight through along the Clutch's shaft axis
Powering the Clutch disconnects the output side and stops transmitted rotation immediately
The same powered state blocks thermochemical heat, making the Clutch a hard cutoff for the entire route
Remove the redstone signal and both rotation and thermochemical heat reconnect through the line
There is no GUI, mode, threshold, storage, or amplification: redstone alone decides whether the route passes or stops
